contents.entry: Mechanism: a script, rclone, a one-time token
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
What this volume needs from the shared volumes

pointers.sibling: Input and output record schema of this node
Spec book check; only a checked book is published
Cleanup registry, which retains this node's manifests
pointers.shared: The repository spec book is the truth (D24)
The book version element the index carries

purpose.is: After every merge that touches rebuild/design, copies the spec book to the owner's Google Drive as immutable, version-named files in a folder named for the book version and the UTC date, and records the file ids, so the owner keeps the Drive reading habit without a second truth (D24 B).
purpose.is-not: It never reads Drive as an input, never overwrites a copy, never publishes an unchecked book, and never runs inside an agent session.
purpose.why: The PROCESS-SEED rule made Drive the truth and the repo the fallback; the Drive then had no factory write after 2026-10-06 and the whole current iteration was absent from it (L15 section 2, D24 facts). The owner's own compaction-guard-publish skill shows the version-named, never-overwritten shape; its defect is that it runs through MCP tools inside a Claude session, which is an agent typing.

input.record: A merge record whose changed paths include rebuild/design/**; the merge sha is the book version's commit.
input.condition: The merge sha has a check.verdict 201 from N-46 (it must, because coq/gate was green to merge; the node verifies the record exists before publishing).

output.record: The folder id, the book version, the merge sha, and one row per published file: repository path, Drive title, file id, bytes, sha256 and md5 of the repository file, and the md5 and sha256 Drive reports (rclone lsjson --hash), equal or not.

A title already in the version folder whose Drive hash differs from the repository file's (reason content-conflict): the copy is not written, not trashed and not overwritten; one owner card names the title, both hashes and the file id (review F24).
Nothing to publish: every title for this version already exists (a re-run after an unknown outcome).
Three attempts failed; the rows that failed and the last error; owner acts only when the error is auth (token revoked or missing), which is the one thing only the owner can fix.
The publisher is not set up (rclone binary or token absent); one owner card the first time, then a counter until it is fixed.

naming.folder: coq spec book v<book-version> <YYYY-MM-DD> <sha7> under the owner's spec book folder (config drive.folder_id, the owner supplies it once at set-up).
naming.title: <path under rebuild/design with slashes replaced by a space-dash-space> v<book-version>.<ext>, for example nodes - N-47 - spec v1.3.0.xml and shared - status-codes v1.3.0.xml.
naming.book-version: index.xml carries book-version; a merge that changes any volume bumps it in the same PR (the value lives in bin/make-index.py); the bump is checked here, at publish, because check.sh in a pod sees one sha and no base: when the version's Drive folder already holds a manifest whose volume hashes differ from this merge's, the publish is drive.copy 423 reason version-not-bumped and N-11 requests a bump ticket; a second publish of the same version with the same hashes finds every title present (204).
naming.immutable: A title that exists in the folder is never written again. A change is a new version with a new folder. A present title counts as published only when its Drive md5 and sha256 equal the repository file's; a present title with a different hash is drive.copy 409 content-conflict and one card, never skipped as present and never overwritten. Nothing is ever trashed by this node except a copy this run created whose hash does not match, inside the same run, before the run is reported (the skill's rule, kept and strengthened from size to hash).
naming.manifest: Every run also uploads manifest v<version>.json and a README v<version>.md that says the repository is the truth and names the merge sha. The manifest has one row per file: repository path, title, bytes, sha256 and md5 of the bytes at the merge sha. sha256 is the book's hash (the one index.xml and the records use); md5 is the hash Drive computes for every binary file, so the comparison needs no download.

mechanism.where: rebuild/design/bin/publish-drive.sh in the repository, run by the service as an Executor.Run verb publish-drive with a 10 minute timeout; it calls rclone (shelf tool, pinned version and sha256 in images.json, installed under $COQ_STATE/bin by the same checksum-verified pattern as the pod binaries) with a Drive remote whose OAuth token lives in $COQ_STATE/secrets/rclone.conf (mode 0600, never in the repository, never in a record).
mechanism.step: Take lease publish:drive (fence, 15 minute expiry). A held lease means another merge is publishing; this run waits on the lease up to its timeout, then re-queues on the next tick (the merge record is still the input; the node keeps a publish cursor of the last published sha in the store).
Verify check.verdict 201 exists for the merge sha; read book-version from index.xml at the merge sha from the mirror; export the book tree at that sha to $COQ_STATE/publish/<sha>/ with git archive.

Compute sha256 and md5 of every exported file into the manifest rows. rclone lsjson the owner folder; create the version folder if absent (rclone mkdir); rclone lsjson --hash --hash-type MD5 --hash-type SHA-256 the version folder for existing titles and their hashes.

For every present title: equal hashes is row present; a different hash is row conflict, and the run ends drive.copy 409 content-conflict with one card (owner acts: the owner decides whether the folder copy or the version number is wrong; the system never writes over it). For every absent title: rclone copyto with --drive-import-formats none (no conversion to Google Docs types; the file stays xml, json, md, sh); then lsjson --hash the title and compare md5 and sha256 with the manifest row; a mismatch on a copy this run created is deleted (rclone deletefile) and retried as part of the three attempts.
Upload manifest and README (hash-checked the same way); write drive.copy 201 with the rows; advance the publish cursor; release the lease.
mechanism.setup-once: The owner authorizes rclone once (rclone config create drive-coq drive scope=drive.file, browser consent on the owner's machine, recorded as a control.action by N-42 with no token in the record); the token refreshes itself. Scope drive.file limits the token to files this app created plus the folder the owner shares with it. This is the only owner step, done once; its absence is the 503 path, never a loop.

diagram.mermaid: flowchart LR M[merge touching rebuild/design] --> V{check.verdict 201 for sha?} V -- no --> X[drive.copy 423 reason unchecked] V -- yes --> L[lease publish:drive] L --> E[git archive at sha] E --> F[rclone lsjson folder, mkdir version folder] F --> C[present titles hash-checked; copyto each missing title; md5 and sha256 compare] C -- all present, hashes equal --> N[drive.copy 204] C -- present title, other hash --> K[drive.copy 409 + one card] C --> R[drive.copy 201 with file ids]

start.s: The merge record from N-09 starts it; the service runs the verb; no agent and no owner action is on the path after the one-time token set-up.

A merge that lands while the publisher is unavailable is not lost: the publish cursor lags the main sha and the daily tick re-runs the node for the newest sha above the cursor, so the Drive catches up to the latest version (older skipped versions are not back-filled, by design; the repository has them).

wait.fallback: re-queue on the next tick; the cursor remembers; no record is lost

wait.what: rclone lsjson, mkdir, copyto per call
wait.fallback: count one attempt of three; then drive.copy 423 with the rows that failed
killed; files already present are fine (immutable titles); the next run skips them (204 or a partial 201)

wait.timeout: none; the system does not wait
wait.fallback: 503 once as a card, then a counter and a Controls lamp; publishing resumes when the token exists; the repository remains the truth throughout

waits.cog-test: The cog that could stall this node is a Claude session with Drive MCP tools (the current skill). rclone under the service removes it; the only human step is one consent click, once.

retries.policy: Per failed file row; successful rows are not re-uploaded (title exists).
retries.recover: After three failures: drive.copy 423, lease released, cursor not advanced; the daily tick retries the newest sha. A 403 or 401 from Drive is classed auth and goes to the owner once.
retries.report: A 423 for a non-auth reason is an alert record (N-41); auth is one card (N-28); a size mismatch that persists three times is a 423 with the row and never a silent bad copy.

many-agents.readers: Any agent may read the Drive copies, but no agent builds from them; a volume's own pointers say the repository path is the truth, and the README in every folder says so.
many-agents.writers: Only the service's verb writes to Drive, under one lease; two merges minutes apart publish in order; a merge that bumps the version while a publish of the previous version runs waits for the lease and then publishes its own folder.
many-agents.collision: Two runs for the same sha (unknown outcome after a kill): the second finds titles present with equal hashes and writes 204; a half-uploaded file (hash mismatch) is deleted and re-uploaded by whichever run holds the lease.

A human creating a file with the same title in the version folder: equal hashes is present; any other content is drive.copy 409 content-conflict and one card naming the title and both hashes; the file is never deleted, because the run did not create it.

Seven spec authors merging seven PRs in one hour: seven version bumps, seven folders, in order; the daily catch-up never skips a merged version while the publisher is healthy, because each merge record is its own trigger.

status-codes.emits: Already published, every hash equal; system acts (nothing).
A present title with a different hash; owner acts (one card); nothing is overwritten.
Failed after 3; system acts (alert, daily retry); owner acts only for reason auth.
Publisher not set up; owner acts once (token), then system counts.

state-paths.path: The git archive export per sha.
Manifest per version (the record holds it too).

path.cleanup: line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry N-47.secret from the owner CLI only (token revoke)

state-paths.path: The token; removed only by the owner from the owner CLI (revoke), never by a timer or a trigger record.
Pinned rclone binaries; the current one is held by a lease while in use.

edges.out: None drawn: drive.copy is a sink; N-28 reads 503 and auth 423 by code; N-40 counts.

item.check: A merge publishes a version folder with one file per volume plus manifest and README.
item.proof: A test against a local rclone remote (rclone serve or the local backend) listing the folder after a merge record; row count equals volume count plus 2; drive.copy 201.

item.check: A second run for the same sha writes nothing and records 204.
item.proof: Run twice; the second record is 204; file count unchanged.

item.check: A hash mismatch on this run's copy is deleted and retried, then reported.
item.proof: A fault-injecting remote that flips one byte once (same size); the row shows one retry and equal md5 and sha256; a remote that always corrupts yields 423 with the row.

item.check: A present title with other content is 409, never skipped or overwritten.
item.proof: A test folder pre-seeded with one title of different bytes; drive.copy 409 content-conflict, one card, the foreign file's id and hash unchanged after the run.

item.check: No token means 503 once and no loop.
item.proof: A test world with no rclone.conf; one drive.copy 503 and one card request; the next tick adds a counter, not a card.

item.check: An unchecked sha is never published.
item.proof: A merge record with no check.verdict 201; drive.copy 423 reason unchecked; no rclone call.

item.check: The token never appears in a record or log.
item.proof: grep of the test world's records and logs for the token string finds nothing.

may.do: run the verb; read the mirror; write under $COQ_STATE/publish; call Drive with the token
authorize the token once; revoke it; read the Drive copies

may-not.do: run publish-drive.sh; read $COQ_STATE/secrets; write to Drive
overwrite or trash a Drive file outside the same run's mismatch rule; count a present title as published without equal hashes; publish an unchecked sha; read Drive as an input

monitoring.counter: Merges touching rebuild/design above the publish cursor; over 0 for 24 hours is an alert.
monitoring.lamp: Green when lag is 0; amber when lag over 0; red on 503 (not set up) or auth 423.

runbook.step: On the host, as the owner: install the pinned rclone (the verb does it from images.json), then rclone config create drive-coq drive scope=drive.file config_is_local=true with the browser consent; move the config to $COQ_STATE/secrets/rclone.conf mode 0600; set drive.folder_id in the service config; the next merge or daily tick publishes.

step.when: the lamp is red for auth

runbook.step: Compare the manifest md5 and sha256 with the Drive hashes in the row; a file with invalid UTF-8 is still copied as bytes by rclone (no conversion), so a persistent mismatch is a Drive-side problem; open the N-41 alert.

The folder holds a title with other bytes: either someone wrote into the version folder (move the file out on Drive, answer the card, the next tick publishes) or the version was not bumped (the bump ticket path); the system never decides which.
The owner runs line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry N-47.secret from the owner CLI; the lamp goes red by design until re-authorized.
runbook.cleanup: line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry N-47.export, N-47.manifests, N-47.log, N-47.bin; N-47.secret only by the owner.
runbook.cold-start: The cursor is in the store; the daily tick publishes the newest version above it.

sources.source: D24 B: repo truth, a script publishes immutable version-named copies as compaction-guard-publish does

Version-named titles, folder per release and date, skip existing titles, size compare after upload, trash only a mismatched copy inside the run, never overwrite, never publish a document whose version does not match the file
Item 23 stable pointer: an artifact bumps only when its content changes; item 7 of section 4: one unversioned INDEX as the commit point
Item 7: hand-written Drive index snapshots by a Sonnet steward
K07 two sources of truth kept in sync
Shelf first: proven open source over own code (rclone)
Digest pins and checksum-verified binaries in images.json, one config

reject.source: $HOME/.claude/skills/compaction-guard-publish/SKILL.md as the runner (MCP Google Drive tools inside a Claude session)
reject.reason: An agent typing; cannot be started by a systemd unit; the naming and the size-compare rules are kept, the runner is rclone under the service.

reject.source: PROCESS-SEED: Drive is the truth, the repo is the fallback
reject.reason: Superseded by D24; a gate can only check what it can read.

reject.source: Google Docs conversion of the volumes
reject.reason: A converted copy is not the bytes the check passed; files stay xml, json and md (rclone --drive-import-formats none).

reject.source: back-filling every skipped version after an outage
reject.reason: The repository holds every version; Drive is a reading surface; the newest version is what the owner reads.

reject.source: a Drive service account with domain-wide delegation
reject.reason: Needs a Workspace domain; the owner's account is a personal Gmail (L15 section 2); OAuth with scope drive.file is the least privilege available.

reject.source: the Drive folder as the publish cursor
reject.reason: Reading Drive to decide what to do makes it an input; the cursor is a store record.

shared-needs.need: principles.xml#repo-is-truth (D24) with the sentence every Drive README carries.
index.xml carries book-version (semver), generated from bin/make-index.py; this node checks the bump at publish (version-not-bumped 423).
publish_cursor: last_published_sha, version, at; leases publish:drive.
drive.copy, merge (with changed paths), control.action (token consent recorded without the token).
201 published, 204 nothing to publish, 409 content-conflict (owner acts, one card), 423 failed after 3 (owner acts only for auth), 503 not set up (owner acts once).
drive.folder_id, drive.remote_name, drive.rclone_version and sha256 in images.json, publish.timeout PT10M.
A $COQ_STATE/secrets convention: mode 0700 directory, 0600 files, listed in the cleanup registry with acts owner, never read by seats (the seat deny list covers the path).
